text:
Extremely dirty here it smells like pee and almost every inch of the area and the music selection for the outside concert was not entertaining in the slightest I went to the Starbucks on the corner to get a frappuccino and was nearly attacked by a transient person who literally pulled my drink out of my hand which I immediately told the Starbucks management about and they replaced the drink for free however the interaction is dangerous to say the least I could have reacted in a less civilized way and mace the individual with complete inpunity

text: Portland spent MILLIONS of dollars "renovating" this place, but they literally didn't change a single thing. And yet the city refuses to meaningfully address the people experiencing homelessness and/or mental distress that use "Portland's living room" as their bedroom. There's tons of boring, commercialized events during the summer, but the city actively discourages citizen art, like talented buskers and artist performances, of which theres no shortage in Portland. Also, absolutely no public restrooms so expect it to smell overwhelmingly like stale piss right outside the overpriced gourmet restaurants geared towards the wealthy bourgeoisie that like to work-live-play in downtown. And there's STILL no memorials to the native people who had their land stolen by the sogcalled pioneers. Pioneer garbage square.
author: Lisa W

text: Lots of aggressive homeless people. I couldn't eat and enjoy a meal outside in peace without several homeless people trying to get money or food from me, but the worst ones were they 3 other ones that asked me repetitively if I wanted heroin & methamphetamine. So discomforting and disgusting! I recommend to take your food and walk around the block to the park out front of PSU, at least there's security and police hovering so there's not aggressive bum's on the prowl for cash or trying to hustle narcotics. Really makes me sad, but would have appreciated a nice peaceful lunch after working all morning and before having to go back to work and finish up.photos from the park I ended up enjoying my lunch in.
author: Daniel Patrick

text: I love the Square but... Pioneer Square should have higher standards for the few food carts that are allowed. They should secret shop each Food cart to do some type of quality check. Amelia's Food cart is terrible, everyone else hits it out of the park! Isn't there anything you can do to have a better quality Mexican food cart there or at the least, talk to the owner and ask them to use spice or salt to season their very bland food and not serve it cold with very runny re-fried beans? Show the tourists that Portland is known for their great food carts! There is a reason why they never have a line to order their food.
author: Renee Chang

text: Used to be such a lively and beautiful destination for tourists and locals alike. Now; every time im down by there, it is HORRIBLE.  Even with events going on. The streets are disgusting and bird crap all over. What happened to city workers cleaning up the sidewalks?? And dont get me started with the scary and demented individuals shouting at nothing and literally accosting individuals! Where's street patrol or STREET OUTREACH that we pay millions for to help get them into services?? Its a shame. My beautiful hometown has lost its sparkle.  Terrifying at night

text: My wife was wanting us to go to Portland so we could see the Christmas Tree at Pioneer Square up close, partly because she often sees it on the news. So for our Saturday outing I drove us out there and the whole thing was blocked off because of the BrewFest and the only way to even get up close to the tree was to pay a fare for the fest. To me if its a public place it shouldn't be blocked off with fees. The fences were even making it hard to see the tree. We left unhappy.
